classification.difficultyReason: Identify corresponding and co-interior angles, combine parallel-line and point-angle properties, and give reasons.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in the diagrams below. Give reasons in each case.

spec.description: Two parallel sloping lines AB and CD cut by transversal SU at T and S; matching arrows and all seven point labels retained.
spec.mathematics: The corresponding sectors at S and T contain 75 degrees and theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 75 degrees and unknown theta are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\theta=75^\circ$$
Corresponding angles are equal because $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Parallel vertical lines PQ and RS crossed by AD at B and C. Both beta labels and matching upward arrows retained; no right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: The two equal co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles are supplementary because $PQ\parallel RS$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta+\beta&=180^\circ\\2\beta&=180^\circ\\\beta&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallel rightward arms AB and CD meet slanted line ACF; 110 degrees at A and 2 alpha below CD at C.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding angles give 2 alpha equal to 110 degrees.

answer.worked:
Corresponding angles are equal because $AB\parallel CD$.
$$\begin{align*}2\alpha&=110^\circ\\\alpha&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Parallel nearly vertical lines AB and CD cut by descending PS at Q and R. Labels 20 degrees, alpha, beta and gamma retain their source sectors. Figure is schematic, as in the source.
spec.mathematics: Alpha is vertically opposite 20 degrees; angle QRD and gamma are 160 degrees; beta is 20 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated angle values are supplied.

answer.short:
$\alpha=20^\circ$, $\beta=20^\circ$, $\gamma=160^\circ$.

Use vertically opposite angles, co-interior angles with $AB\parallel CD$, and supplementary angles.
answer.worked:
$$\alpha=20^\circ$$
Vertically opposite angles at $Q$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\angle QRD&=180^\circ-20^\circ\\\angle QRD&=160^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles are supplementary because $AB\parallel CD$.
$$\gamma=160^\circ$$
Vertically opposite angles at $R$ are equal.
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-160^\circ\\\beta&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles on the straight line $CD$ add to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral LMON with LM parallel NO, matching rightward arrows and equal beta labels at L and N. No right-angle markers.
spec.mathematics: Equal co-interior angles on transversal LN sum to 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Both unknown angles remain labelled beta.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles are supplementary because $LM\parallel NO$.
$$\begin{align*}\beta+\beta&=180^\circ\\2\beta&=180^\circ\\\beta&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
